explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares GPT-4 judgments with human evaluations on the same set of instances for personalization quality assessment, reporting inter-rater reliability between human and LLM evaluators.

prompts.notes: Appendix I contains prompts used for dataset generation, but specific prompts for LLM evaluation are not explicitly shown. Evaluation questions are described in Appendix G.1.

guidelines.notes: Appendix G.1 provides detailed evaluation questions and 4-point Likert scale options for naturalness, fluency, style alignment, content preservation, personalization, semantic consistency, and user experience.

sample_size.notes: Same 100 dialogues were evaluated by both human evaluators and GPT-4

quantitative_scores.notes: Inter-rater correlation between GPT-4 and human evaluators across all five evaluation questions

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 achieved high inter-rater reliability (α=0.84) with human evaluators, closely matching the human inter-annotator agreement of 0.85, indicating strong alignment between LLM and human judgments.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluated the same five criteria for personalization quality assessment, while human evaluators additionally conducted comparative evaluations against baseline methods.
